text:
ryan: Hey team — after bumping the python SDK to 0.12.0 our streaming call blows up in CI. Locally works fine. Error: AttributeError: 'SyncClient' object has no attribute 'send_stream'

maya-support: can you paste the traceback and how you installed the SDK? poetry/pip/venv?

ryan: Using poetry. pyproject snippet: ```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.10"
redwood-inference = "^0.12.0"
httpx = "==0.23.3"
```
CI uses the lockfile. Traceback: ```
File "/app/main.py", line 42, in handle
  client.stream_chat(... )
AttributeError: 'SyncClient' object has no attribute 'send_stream'
```

pip-bot: heads up — some streaming helpers were moved behind the [stream] extra in 0.12.x and require newer httpx/httpcore versions.

eng-nile: quick guess: your pinned httpx (0.23.3) pulls an httpcore that doesn't support the async plumbing we switched to for streaming. That would explain local vs CI if local has a different resolved httpx/httpcore. Can you `pip freeze` from CI?

ryan: pasted pip freeze from CI: ```
redwood-inference==0.12.0
httpx==0.23.3
httpcore==0.16.3
anyio==3.7.0
```

maya-support: thanks. Two things to try: 1) install the streaming extra: `pip install "redwood-inference[stream]"` (or add extras = ["stream"] in pyproject) 2) relax the exact httpx pin so resolver can pick httpx/httpcore >= the versions we test against (we recommend httpx>=0.24 and httpcore>=0.17 for 0.12.x).

sre-liz: also confirm there's no local filename `redwood.py` or package shadowing in repo — that can surface weird attr errors but trace looks like a real mismatch.

ryan: tried quick repro in an isolated venv: recreated with `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install redwood-inference==0.12.0` then ran the snippet that calls streaming and saw same AttributeError. After `pip install "redwood-inference[stream]"` error changed to: `RuntimeError: httpcore backend unsupported: AsyncIOBackend not available`

eng-nile: that next error is consistent with an httpcore mismatch. Run `pip install "httpx>=0.24" "httpcore>=0.17"` or remove the `==0.23.3` pin in pyproject.lock and let poetry/resolver upgrade transitive deps.

ryan: ok I bumped httpx/httpcore in CI and added the extra in pyproject. Rebuilt the lockfile and re-ran. Streaming call now proceeds (I see frames flowing). :tada:

maya-support: awesome — summary for the thread: streaming feature moved behind the [stream] extra in 0.12.x and also relies on newer httpx/httpcore; pinned older httpx in your lockfile prevented the correct backend from being installed. Recommended: add extras = ["stream"] and avoid strict pinned httpx unless you also upgrade httpcore.

ryan: thanks all, gonna push the lockfile change and monitor.

eng-nile: if you want, attach the `poetry.lock` diff and we can double-check no other transitive libs got downgraded.

ryan: will do. thanks!
